b.d: Minnesota conglomerate whose safety arm owns Peltor hearing protection, Speedglas welding filters and Aura/6000 respirators.
Hartford firm whose 'Allen' safety set screw gave the hex key its common name; now Apex Tool Group.
Minden maker of sliding table saws, founded in Berlin by Wilhelm Altendorf.
Founded in Sheffield by pattern maker Ashley Iles; now a family firm in Lincolnshire.
Atlas Press Company of Kalamazoo, Michigan; made Craftsman lathes for Sears until 1981.
Saint-Juéry maker of hand-cut rasps and rifflers; factory closed in 2007.
Enköping hand-tool maker (adjustable wrench, saws, files); part of Snap-on's SNA Europe.
Oregon City knife maker begun as Bali-Song in California; holds the AXIS lock licence.
German clamp maker founded by Max Bessey as a cold-drawn steel mill; originator of the F-style and parallel clamp.
American power-tool brand, now part of Stanley Black & Decker; made the Workmate folding bench.
Small maker of marking knives, chisels and layout tools.
Oyonnax eyewear maker founded by Séraphin Bollé; Bollé Safety is part of Bollé Brands.
Maker that invented the ball-end hex key in 1964.
German group whose power-tool division sells green DIY and blue Professional lines.
Box-Ford lathes from Box Tree Mills, Halifax, begun by Denford Machine Tools.
Bridgeport, Connecticut maker of the turret mill; Textron from 1968, Hardinge from 2004.
Providence, Rhode Island firm that mass-marketed the micrometer caliper; now a Hexagon brand made by TESA.
American knife maker begun by Hoyt Buck in San Diego, now in Post Falls, Idaho.
Californian mining-equipment firm whose 1919 Hard-Boiled hat began the hard hat.
Maker of Shapeoko and Nomad CNC machines; Shapeoko creator Edward Ford joined in 2014.
W. R. Case & Sons of Bradford, Pennsylvania, owned by Zippo; collected by pattern and tang stamp.
Meadville, Pennsylvania plier maker founded by George B. DeArment; originator of modern tongue-and-groove pliers.
Knife maker founded in Durban, later based in the United States; originator of the Integral Lock.
Sheffield maker of shoulder, rebate and bench planes.
Thiers cutler making the Douk-Douk since 1929.
Maker of twin-bar bed lathes; the name now belongs to Record Power.
Lake Waccamaw, North Carolina maker of drop-forged American axe patterns.
Jamestown brand whose adjustable wrench made 'Crescent wrench' generic; now Apex Tool Group.
Sheffield maker of woodturning tools.
Milwaukee-founded machinery brand; Rockwell, Pentair and Black & Decker owned it before Chang Type bought it in 2011.
Stanley Black & Decker's professional power-tool brand, based in Towson, Maryland.
Plattling-based tool house selling Japanese tools under its own name.
Philadelphia saw maker founded by Henry Disston as the Keystone Saw Works; moved to Tacony in 1871; later owned by H.K. Porter.
Diamond Machining Technology, Marlborough, Massachusetts maker of diamond plates.
Racine-founded rotary-tool brand owned by Bosch since 1993.
Sheffield brand from James Neill (trademark 1909); first composite steel hacksaw blade 1911, hacksaw frames from 1924; now with Spear & Jackson.
Cordless outdoor power equipment brand built on a 56V battery.
German DIY tool maker based in Landau/Isar.
German maker credited with the plunge router, now part of DeWalt.
Maier & Co. of Austria, maker of the Unimat miniature machine tool.
Golden, Colorado maker of CO2 laser engravers; claims the first small-format laser engraving system.
Swedish welding and cutting equipment maker.
Rockford, Illinois maker founded by Ernest Estwing; first to sell hammers forged from one piece of solid steel.
German power-tool maker, originator of the oscillating multi-tool.
Felder Group of Hall in Tyrol, family maker of combination machines and panel saws; brands Hammer and Format4.
German maker of system-based premium tools for woodworkers.
Finnish tool and homeware group, maker of composite-handled X-series axes.
Erie, Pennsylvania maker founded as Falls Run Woodcarving; tools from 1992.
Boden knife firm founded by Peter Hjortberger, making laminated-steel knives in Japan.
Remscheid maker of spanners, sockets and torque tools founded by the Dowidat brothers.
Portland, Oregon knife and multi-tool brand owned by Fiskars.
Californian maker of the Tite-Mark marking gauge.
Crowdfunded maker of camera-guided desktop laser cutters for home crafters.
Minneapolis maker of airless and other paint sprayers for DIY and trade.
American hand-tool maker (Tools for Working Wood) of cold-formed steel holdfasts and saws.
Swedish forge making signed hand-forged axes.
Japanese maker of Razorsaw replaceable-blade pull saws.
British decorating-tools brand with tiered ranges (For The Trade, Prestige, Perfection).
Felder Group's affordable brand for home woodworkers and small businesses.
American precision lathe maker, early machines sold as Cataract; owner of Bridgeport from 2004.
L.G. Harris & Co of Stoke Prior near Bromsgrove, the largest UK maker of decorating brushes; owned by Orkla since 2016.
Liechtenstein maker of construction tools sold direct.
Conglomerate whose safety division sells North respirators and Uvex eyewear in the Americas.
Swedish forge founded in 1697, making axes as a main line since the 1870s.
Swedish maker of chainsaws, garden machinery and forestry protective clothing.
Swiss maker of jewelled lever-type dial test indicators.
Chicago company that sold Shapeoko kits, then its own X-Carve machines and Easel software.
American hand-tool brand whose Quick-Grip line began the one-handed bar clamp.
JPW Industries machinery brand alongside Powermatic.
Chicago clamp brand of the Adjustable Clamp Company (later Pony Tools); revived in 2018 under GreatStar.
Portland knife brand founded by Pete Kershaw, owned by Kai since 1977; SpeedSafe with Ken Onion.
Cast-iron kindling splitter invented in New Zealand, made in Australia.
Remscheid family firm whose tools carry the Two Cherries mark.
Chicago-founded maker of electricians' tools whose name became generic for lineman's pliers.
Maker of truss-frame aluminium and titanium fret and coping saws, developed by machinist Lee Marshall and now owned by Brian Meek.
Family-owned Wuppertal plier maker founded by Carl Gustav Putsch.
Laguna Tools, begun in Laguna Beach, California, now based in Grand Prairie, Texas.
Swiss company founded by Hermann Steiner, inventor of the biscuit joint.
Portland, Oregon maker founded by Tim Leatherman; originator of the plier multi-tool.
Family-owned Warren, Maine maker of bronze and ductile-iron planes based on traditional Stanley designs.
Cleveland, Ohio welding-equipment maker.
American maker of rules, tapes and test indicators.
British maker of Mole grips from 1955.
Maker of the Carvera desktop CNC mill with automatic tool changer.
Japanese power-tool maker based in Anjō.
US trowel maker; a preferred American brand of pointing trowel.
Sanjo, Niigata kiridashi workshop, now run by second-generation smith Yoshihide Masuda.
German power-tool maker from Nürtingen, initiator of the CAS alliance.
Miller Electric of Appleton, Wisconsin, welding-equipment maker owned by ITW.
Massachusetts hand-tool maker, best known for braces and hand drills; owned by Ingersoll Rand from 1962 and the name by Great Star since 2002.
Brookfield, Wisconsin tool maker owned by TTI since 2005.
Italian combination-machine brand of the SCM Group.
Kawasaki-based metrology maker that began with micrometers and added digital gauging from the 1970s.
US maker of disposable and reusable respirators and earplugs.
Sheffield toolmaker founded by Frank Moore; made micrometers from 1930; sold to Bower Metrology UK in 2000.
Mora, Dalarna maker formed from KJ Eriksson and Frosts.
Mine Safety Appliances, founded by John T. Ryan Sr. and George Deike; now MSA Safety of Cranberry Township, Pennsylvania.
Founded by Cecil Moore in Beeston, Nottinghamshire; since 2011 Myford Ltd of Mytholmroyd.
Miki factory making higonokami knives under the KaneKoma brand.
Japanese waterstone maker.
Czech maker of chisels and woodworking hand tools.
London maker of infill planes whose 1913 adjuster made it the leading 20th-century infill maker; ended early 1950s.
Philadelphia maker of Yankee spiral ratchet screwdrivers, push drills, hand drills and braces; bought by Stanley in 1946.
Worcester, Massachusetts abrasives maker, owned by Saint-Gobain since 1990.
Italian fastener firm; Egidio Brugola patented a spiral-shank hex key in 1946.
Osaka maker founded by Yoshio Okada, originator of the snap-off blade.
Maker of heavy welded-bed woodturning lathes (2000 Series).
Savoie maker of beech-handled numbered folding knives with the Virobloc collar.
Family-owned Swiss maker of professional hand tools, making screwdrivers since 1940.
Peter Wright and Sons of Dudley and Oldbury, anvil and vice makers; solid anvil 1852.
French maker of climbing and work-at-height equipment and headlamps.
Swiss maker of carving tools sold as 'Swiss Made'.
Tennessee machinery maker founded in McMinnville; a JPW Industries brand since 2008.
Portland, Oregon maker of hand-made paint brushes, owned by Sherwin-Williams.
US maker of budget safety glasses, hard hats and hearing protection; Venture Gear is its outdoor line.
Chinese maker of Bedrock-pattern bench planes and joinery planes with T10 irons.
Sheffield maker (C. & J. Hampton) of Stanley-pattern planes and vices.
Sheffield maker of hobby woodworking machines, owner of Coronet, Burgess and CamVac; Startrite is its industrial brand.
Emerson-owned US tool brand from Ohio whose power tools are made largely by TTI.
Sheffield edge-tool maker first registered in Union Street in 1828.
Robland-Landuyt of Bruges, maker of combination machines first aimed at hobby woodworkers.
Robust Tools, American lathe maker owned by Brent English.
Spanish maker of manual tile cutters and tiling tools.
Japanese-origin brand; its power tools are made under licence by TTI.
Swedish steel maker (Sandvikens Jernverk) that introduced the tubular steel bow saw; its saws and tools business passed to Bahco.
Tualatin, Oregon maker of flesh-sensing table saws; owned by TTS Tooltechnic (Festool) since 2017.

b.d: Ichenhausen, Bavaria maker of DIY and workshop woodworking machines; Woodster range from 2005.
Niigata smith who hand-makes kanna such as the Chizoku hira-ganna.
Japanese maker of glass-backed and other ceramic waterstones.
Sherline Products, incorporated in the USA by Joe Martin; design from Australia's Harold Clisby and Ron Sher.
Japanese maker of rules and squares including sashigane.
SIEG Industrial Group of Shanghai, maker of most mini mills sold under importer brands.
Japanese saw maker founded by Katsuji Miyawaki.
Swedish workbench maker known for joiner's benches and the portable Smart Vice.
Kenosha tool maker that began with snap-on interchangeable sockets; sells lower-end tools as Blue-Point.
South Bend Lathe Works of South Bend, Indiana.
Sheffield maker of saws, hand and garden tools, tracing to Spear & Love (1760); owns the Eclipse brand; SNH Global since 2014.
Golden, Colorado knife maker founded by Sal Glesser, known for the round opening hole.
New Britain, Connecticut toolmaker (Stanley Rule & Level) whose numbered Bailey planes set the standard plane pattern.
Athol, Massachusetts maker founded by Laroy S. Starrett, inventor of the combination square.
Waiblingen chainsaw maker that also sells forestry protective clothing.
Maker of Japanese hand planes using traditional kanna-making methods.
US maker of the Taig micro lathe and mill, sold in the UK as Peatol.
Teknatool International, maker of Nova lathes, chucks and DVR direct-drive machines.
Renens metrology maker, Brown & Sharpe group from 1967, Hexagon 2001–2024, GreatStar since 2024; absorbed Etalon and others.
Sheffield saw maker whose flagship range is Pax backsaws, made by long-established hand methods.
Swedish wet-grinder maker founded by Torgny Jansson.
British router and cutter specialist.
Fürth maker of goggles and safety eyewear; sold in the Americas through Honeywell.
Manufacturing arm of Lee Valley Tools, Ottawa, making planes, gauges and sharpening tools.
Ibach knife maker founded by Karl Elsener; absorbed Wenger in 2005.
German maker of DIY and professional paint spraying equipment.
Delémont-area supplier of Swiss Army knives, bought by Victorinox in 2005; knife brand merged into Victorinox in 2013.
Wuppertal screwdriver and hand-tool maker; owned by Bitburger Holding since 2016.
Axe factory in Storvik, Sweden.
Black Forest screwdriver and hand-tool maker founded by Willi Hahn; screwdrivers since 1947.
Chicago vice maker founded by Hugh W. Vogl, known for the bullet vise; part of JPW Industries.
Sharpener brand of Darex, made in Ashland, Oregon.
Shenzhen laser brand associated with Makeblock.
Zetsaw brand of Okada Hardware Mfg., pioneer of replaceable handsaw blades and impulse-hardened teeth.
Knife maker that grew from Randall's Adventure & Training survival school, known for numbered 1095 fixed blades.
Fixed-blade maker whose Becker line, designed by Ethan Becker, includes the BK2 Companion.
Maker of pressurised-cartridge pens developed by Paul C. Fisher, patented 1965.
Maker of machined aluminium tactical pens with pressurised cartridges.
Maker of keyring accessories including the DoohicKey tool.
Iowa maker of the Kreg Jig, founded by Craig Sommerfeld.
Maker of the Leigh D4R Pro router dovetail jig, part of Lee Valley Tools.
Pennsylvania maker whose 1946 gun was the first instant-heating soldering gun, and whose Magnastat iron followed in 1960.
Maker of the open-source Pinecil USB-C soldering iron.
German maker of portable woodworking machines, based in Oberndorf.
Brand of Koki Holdings, formerly Hitachi Koki, bought by KKR in 2017; sold as Metabo HPT in the US.
Steinheim maker of the first angle grinder; the name 'Flex' is German slang for one.
Franchise-sold professional hand tool and toolbox brand, owned by Vontier.
Franchise-sold professional hand tool and storage brand owned by Stanley Black & Decker.
Wuppertal maker of forged hand tools for automotive, industrial and aerospace use.
Remscheid maker of about six thousand tools, including torque tools and Assistent tool trolleys.
Family-owned Dayton, Ohio maker of wooden tool chests, including machinists' chests.
